purpose: Figure 1 FastRelax series rerun with torsion-space (atom-tree / kinematic) relax; all earlier Figure 1 FastRelax runs used Cartesian relax.

tmol.release: uw-ipd/tmol v0.2.0 (2026-10-20), includes #602 'restore kin relax' (KinematicMinimizer / DefaultKinematicMinimizer)
tmol.software: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132 (container), CUDA runtime 13.2, tmol ops built for CUDA 13; AtomWorks 3.0.4 (required by tmol 0.2.0; the 0.1.58 run used 2.1.1/git); see metadata/pip-freeze.txt
tmol.unmerged_branches_used: none (PRs #614/#615 not needed: #602 is merged and released in v0.2.0)

relax_definitions.tmol_torsion: tmol.relax.fast_relax(num_repeats=1, default MonomerRelax2019 schedule) with min_fn=DefaultKinematicMinimizer(cuda_graph=True on CUDA, False on CPU), MoveMap.from_pose_stack with move_all_jumps=True and move_all_named_torsions=True (all backbone/side-chain/ligand torsions and non-root jumps; bond lengths and angles fixed), FoldForest.reasonable_fold_forest, score function beta2016 (unchanged), seed 20260906. Same recipe as tmol's own test_kin_fast_relax_ubq.
relax_definitions.tmol_cartesian_control: same harness, fast_relax default Cartesian minimizer (CartesianMoveMap, graph mode auto) on tmol 0.2.0, to separate the torsion effect from the 0.1.58->0.2.0 version change.
relax_definitions.pyrosetta_torsion: protocols.relax.FastRelax(sfxn, 1) with MonomerRelax2019 script lines, cartesian(False), MoveMap bb=chi=jump=True; sfxn beta_nov16 (protein, protein-nucleic) / beta_genpot (protein-ligand). Differs from the Cartesian runs only by pro_close 1.25 instead of 0 and no cart_bonded 0.5 (diff of the weight files).
relax_definitions.scoring_difference_note: tmol keeps its cart_* bonded terms and has no pro_close in torsion mode; PyRosetta torsion drops cart_bonded and adds pro_close. Final energies of the two engines are therefore not directly comparable (they were not exactly comparable before either).

timing_contract: unchanged from the Cartesian run: one seeded one-repeat FastRelax per point, input/scorer/move-map construction outside the timed interval, no warm-up (first-call JIT and kernel-loading costs are inside the interval, for both modes), GPU synchronised before the final clock read, one process per point; seconds/structure = batch seconds / batch size.
systems: same 12 tmol systems and 27 PyRosetta inputs as the Cartesian matrix (matrix.json)
loader_note: tmol 0.2.0 renamed pose_stack_from_pdb/_biotite; harness uses pose_stack_from_file / pose_stack_from_atom_array with identical options. Protein/NA initial scores match the 0.1.58 run; protein-ligand initial scores differ (e.g. hsp90 386.1 vs 312.7) because tmol 0.2.0 prepares ligands differently, so old-vs-new tmol energies are not comparable for ligand systems - use the same-version Cartesian control.
nodes_note: per-point node, GPU, CPU model and Slurm job id are in each results/raw JSON under machine; GPU and CPU array tasks of this run (and of the control) may share a node with each other
old_run_incompleteness: the figure data snapshot of the Cartesian run was 68/87 complete (10 tmol GPU B1000 points and 9 PyRosetta points pending); the raw directory later holds all 87 files and the comparison uses those

optimisation_experiments.note: scratch patches to tmol (v0.2.0 and master 1fbd25f34); not part of the Figure 1 numbers; JIT-compiled kernels; SA trajectory budget reduced to 100 (env var), numba cache, trusted fold forest, value-only line search
